neighbours.label: The word ' vein(s)' in its literal, physical sense: blood veins, leaf veins, ore/mineral veins, marble veining; not the idiom 'in the same vein' and not look-alikes (vain, veneer)
neighbours.notes: Probes: neck/leaf/marble veins 1.0-1.24, ore vein 1.07, varicose veins 0.68; idiom 'in the same vein' 0.08, 'in vain' 0.01, 'veneer' 0.06. Related words fire weakly (arteries 0.32, streaks 0.39, vessels 0.23, capillaries 0.21), so those are kept out of the near misses. Nerve sentences mostly <0.1. Feeds the L9 nerve neuron (single-unit zero-ablation drop 0.10, measured on the whole unit; the + pole of this unit already has a record).
fire: The nurse found a good vein in the back of his hand.
Thick blue veins stood out on the old man's forearms.
The prospectors struck a narrow vein of silver in the hillside.
Hold the leaf up to the light and you can see its fine veins.
The white countertop is crossed by delicate grey veins.
A blood clot formed in a deep vein of her leg.
His temple vein throbbed as he shouted at the referee.
Quartz veins cut through the dark granite of the cliff.
quiet: The nurse found a good spot on the back of his hand.
Thick blue tattoos stood out on the old man's forearms.
The prospectors found a small deposit of silver in the hillside.
Hold the leaf up to the light and you can see its fine hairs.
The white countertop is marked by a few small scratches.
A painful cramp formed in the lower part of her leg.
In a similar vein, the coach complained about the referee.
She waited in vain for the rock samples from the cliff.
